correctness.rationale: The full infinite proof gives a reversible edge-labelled two-arc contraction, rank-one matrix-tree ratio, explicit nilpotent-resolvent overlap sum and exact classification of d0=0,-1,-2. Uniform geometric bounds and a closed alternating sum give sharp minima/maxima and unique equality families at every q>=3,n>=2. Separate successor-permutation and full determinant code verifies finite examples and equality cases. Constant words are correctly excluded.

broader_coverage.reasoning: These general distribution/count formulas can yield the single-pattern probability, so merely expressing that marginal differently is not original. A stronger published *extremal* statement would cover the present theorem; its possible presence in uninspected general-distribution appendices is a residual risk.

The earlier support-only result determines whether a marginal vanishes, not these positive probabilities.

originality.rationale: This finding claims only the sharp universal nonbinary probability envelope and full extremizer classification, not the general expected-count formula already proved by Cowan or the prior support classification. The 2025 unbiased-sampler primary paper, full Cowan 1991 theorem and accessible related count literature do not state this all-parameter optimization. residual_risks: An all-order sharp optimization might be an unnoticed corollary or appendix of an earlier general Markov pattern-count formula.

Database and publication searches cannot certify absolute novelty; specialized or unindexed literature may overlap.

value.rationale: An order-independent strictly positive lower probability for every nonconstant next-order word, together with all equality cases, is a motivated sharp sampling-coverage invariant for uniformly generated de Bruijn cycles. The exact worst-case sampling probability yields a concrete all-pattern union bound; it is neither a fixed small table nor a change of notation.
